questions.question_text: At what type of financial institution must a WV broker maintain a trust fund account?
questions.correct_answer: One insured against loss by a federal agency
distractors: Any financial institution located in West Virginia
A state-chartered commercial bank only
An institution specifically chartered by the WVREC
questions.explanation: Each trust fund account "shall be established at a financial institution which is insured against loss by an agency of the federal government and the amount deposited therein cannot exceed the amount that is insured against loss" (§30-40-18(c)). The test is federal insurance, not FDIC specifically — an NCUA-insured credit union qualifies too.

questions.question_text: What type of deposit account must a WV broker's trust account be?
distractors: A 30-day notice savings account
A certificate of deposit (CD)
A money market account with restrictions
questions.explanation: Trust accounts must allow for withdrawal without notice (demand deposit). This ensures funds can be disbursed promptly when needed for transactions.

questions.question_text: Under what conditions may WV trust funds be held in an interest-bearing account?
questions.correct_answer: Only under a written agreement of all parties, and never for the broker's benefit
distractors: Never — interest-bearing trust accounts are forbidden outright
Any time the broker chooses, with the interest belonging to the broker
Any time, provided the interest is split with the responsible broker
questions.explanation: Interest is barred "unless specifically authorized by commission rule" (§30-40-18(e)), and that authorization comes on strict conditions: a written agreement from all parties to the transaction authorizing the transfer, identifying the institution and account type, identifying who will earn the interest, and stating how and when it will be disbursed (174-1-15.4). No interest or other benefit from such an account may go to the broker or any other licensee, and on closing the account the total proceeds must return to the broker's trust fund account before any disbursement.

questions.question_text: A WV broker receives $300,000 in trust funds. The FDIC insurance limit is $250,000 per depositor. What should the broker do?
questions.correct_answer: Distribute funds across multiple trust accounts
distractors: Deposit all funds in one account anyway
Return the excess to the client
Invest the excess in a separate portfolio
questions.explanation: The amount in any one trust account is capped at the federally insured amount (§30-40-18(c)). 174-1-15.5 gives brokers with excess funds two compliant routes: multiple trust accounts at various financial institutions, or a cash sweep account established at an institution that has a Trust Fund Account Statement and Consent to Examine on file. The sweep route requires a Commission-prescribed addendum signed by the broker and the institution, filed with the Commission within 10 business days.

questions.question_text: A broker opens a new trust account. Within how many days must they notify the WVREC?
distractors: 5 days
30 days
60 days
questions.explanation: The broker must notify the commission within 10 days of establishing or changing a trust fund account. This allows WVREC to maintain oversight of all active trust accounts.

questions.question_text: Absent contrary direction in the signed purchase agreement, when must a WV broker deposit trust funds into the trust account?
questions.correct_answer: Immediately or by the next business day after receipt
distractors: Promptly, with no specific deadline set by rule
Within five business days after receipt
Within 10 days after receipt
questions.explanation: The deadline is hard: "Unless otherwise directed or allowed in the signed purchase agreement, every broker who receives any trust funds shall immediately or by the next business day following receipt deposit the trust funds in the broker's trust account" (174-1-15.3). The same clock applies one step earlier — under 174-1-15.2 a salesperson or associate broker who receives trust funds must pay them over to the responsible broker immediately or by the next business day.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT considered a trust fund that must go into a WV broker's trust account?
questions.correct_answer: The broker's earned commission after closing
distractors: Earnest money deposits from the buyer
Security deposits collected from tenants
Auction proceeds held pending settlement
questions.explanation: The broker's earned commission is personal income, not trust funds. Trust funds include earnest money, security deposits, rental receipts, auction proceeds, and money held in escrow.

questions.question_text: A WV broker deposits their personal funds into the trust account to cover operating expenses. What violation has occurred?
distractors: No violation if the amount is small
Unauthorized practice of banking
A trust account balance violation
questions.explanation: Commingling is the mixing of personal funds with trust funds. A broker may only maintain a nominal amount of personal funds to keep the account open; depositing personal funds for business use is prohibited.

questions.question_text: Can a WV broker keep any personal funds in a trust account?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, a maximum of $100 to maintain a minimum balance
distractors: No, absolutely no personal funds are allowed
Yes, up to $500 for operating costs
Yes, up to 10% of the trust fund balance
questions.explanation: Commingling is prohibited, with a precise exception: "nothing contained herein prevents the broker from depositing a maximum of $100 of his or her own money in the trust fund account to maintain a minimum balance in the account" (§30-40-18(f)). §30-40-18(i)(7) reinforces the figure by making the bank certify that it does not require a minimum balance above the amount subsection (f) allows.

questions.question_text: A property manager collects rental payments on behalf of a landlord. Where should these funds be deposited?
distractors: The property manager's personal account
The landlord's personal bank account
A general business operating account
questions.explanation: Rental receipts must go into a trust fund account, along with earnest money deposits, security deposits, auction proceeds and money held in escrow at closing (§30-40-18(b)). Under 174-1-15.2 a salesperson or associate broker who takes in those funds must deliver them to the responsible broker immediately or by the next business day, and the broker must deposit them on the same clock (174-1-15.3).

questions.question_text: What must a financial institution certify regarding a WV broker's trust account?
questions.correct_answer: The exact account title and agree to notify WVREC of bounced checks
distractors: That the account earns a minimum interest rate
That the broker has a minimum credit score
That the account has a minimum daily balance
questions.explanation: The Commission-prepared statement must contain the exact title of the account as registered by the institution, the account number, identification of all persons authorized to make withdrawals, the institution's name and address, the title of the person signing for the institution, the date of execution, and certification both that the institution will notify the Commission of any checks returned for insufficient funds and that it does not require a minimum balance above the amount §30-40-18(f) allows (§30-40-18(i)).

questions.question_text: A broker changes the financial institution where their trust account is held. What must they do?
distractors: No notification is required
Notify the WVREC within 30 days
Get WVREC approval before the change
questions.explanation: A broker must notify the commission within 10 days of establishing or changing a trust fund account. The new financial institution must also execute the commission-prepared certification statement.

questions.question_text: The WVREC requests copies of a broker's trust account records from the bank. Can the bank provide them?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, the broker authorized commission access
distractors: No, banking records are private
Only with a court order
Only during a formal investigation
questions.explanation: Brokers must authorize periodic WVREC inspections of trust accounts, and the commission can obtain copies of records from the financial institution. This authorization is a condition of licensure.

questions.question_text: What happens when a trust account check from a WV broker bounces at the financial institution?
questions.correct_answer: The bank must notify the WVREC
distractors: The bank reprocesses the check automatically
The broker has 5 days to cover it privately
Nothing happens unless a complaint is filed
questions.explanation: The financial institution has agreed to notify the WVREC if any trust account checks are returned for insufficient funds. This triggers the commission's investigation process.

questions.question_text: A WV broker opens a trust account at a new bank. What document must the bank execute?
distractors: A broker liability waiver form
A standard banking agreement only
An FDIC insurance application form
questions.explanation: The financial institution must execute a commission-prepared statement certifying the exact account title and agreeing to notify the WVREC if any trust account checks bounce.
